note: The four flag states WITHOUT the orchestrator flag were recorded from index.js at commit bc718e06, before the orchestrator capabilities existed. Read that scope exactly: bc718e06 is a commit on the mcp-orchestration branch, NOT the deployed 1.1.1 tree, so this fixture is evidence that the listing has not moved SINCE IT WAS RECORDED — it is not evidence that it equals what the review connection is served. Between f753a8ca and bc718e06 the branch added get_bank_spending_summary, search_bank_transactions and attach_bank_receipt, corrected six annotation values across four tools (update_order_status twice, update_note twice, pin_note once, archive_note once) and changed "Lite" to "Starter" in two descriptions; all of those are intended 1.2.0 changes, listed in docs/mcp-submission-1.2.0.md section 3. Name commits, never "the merge base": this branch has two. f753a8ca is git merge-base HEAD main; 015d5792 is the merge base with the deploy branch macbook-save-before-macstudio-2026-06-01, and only that one was ever deployed. The changes listed above are real relative to f753a8ca and irrelevant to a parity question for that reason. Measured against 015d5792 the flags-off wire did not move by a byte, and states.off.tools here is byte-identical to the reconstructed production listing (docs/mcp-production-parity.md) — so the caveat above is discharged against the deployed SOURCE. The operator still diffs this fixture against the live listing once before the flip, which is the one thing a source-level reconstruction cannot stand in for. The two orchestrator states are a different kind of record: they are the 1.2.0 PROPOSAL, re-recorded whenever it deliberately changes, and they are compared by mcp-tools-list-snapshot.test.js like the other four. They were compared by nothing until 6 Sep 2026 and went stale: the inventory+orchestrator state carried a recording with both search_inventory and search_inventory_items in it — the duplicate inventory search 70c474fd removed — while the builder published only one of them. Both were re-recorded then, and again when the reduction of 6 Sep 2026 took eight capabilities out of the release; they hold 21 tools and 22 tools now, search_inventory only. The figures the fold and the reduction moved through are in docs/mcp-inventory-search-decision.md section 5. Re-recorded a third time on 7 Sep 2026, when the operator took every monetary field out of the two kept capabilities: the tool COUNTS did not move (21 and 22, search_inventory only), and the only wire change is search_commerce_orders description, which promised "connection, totals and last sync all stay distinct fields" over an answer that no longer carries a total, a currency or any other amount. Re-record with: node test/qa/mcp-tools-list-snapshot.test.js --write, which touches ONLY those two states; the four flag-off recordings are evidence about a pre-orchestrator listing and regenerating them would destroy the only thing they prove.

tools.description: Summarise the connected workspace's business bank feed (Open Banking) for a month or a year: total spent, incoming, change vs the previous period, spending by category, top merchants and recurring subscriptions. tools.title: Search bank transactions
tools.description: List individual bank transactions from the connected workspace's bank feed, filtered by keyword (merchant/description), date range, category, amount range, or missing receipt. Returns the newest first. Requires the Bank Spending permission. Do not ask for companyId.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

query.description: Keyword matched against merchant and description, e.g. amazon, openai.

category.description: Category name as shown in NivaDesk, e.g. Materials, Software, Shipping; use Uncategorised for transactions without a category.

direction.description: out = spending (default), in = incoming, all = both.

withoutReceipt.description: true = only spending that has no receipt/invoice attached yet.

limit.description: Max rows to return (default 20).

tools.name: attach_bank_receipt
tools.title: Attach receipt to a bank transaction
tools.description: Attach an invoice/receipt the user shared in the chat to the matching bank transaction in NivaDesk. Pass the user's file as `receipt`. NivaDesk OCRs images itself; for PDFs (or to help matching) also pass the total amount, the document date (YYYY-MM-DD) and the merchant name you read from the document. If NivaDesk finds one confident match it attaches the file immediately; if several transactions could match it returns candidates with an inboxPath — show them to the user, then call again with the chosen transactionId and the same inboxPath (no need to resend the file). Workspace owner only. Do not ask for companyId.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

receipt.description: The invoice/receipt file the user attached (image or PDF).

inboxPath.description: Returned by a previous call when several candidates matched; pass it back together with transactionId instead of resending the file.

transactionId.description: Bank transaction to attach to, when the user has chosen one of the candidates (or named the transaction).

amount.description: Total amount printed on the document, if you can read it.

date.description: Document/payment date YYYY-MM-DD, if you can read it.

merchant.description: Merchant/supplier name on the document, if you can read it.

tools.name: attach_bank_receipt
tools.title: Attach receipt to a bank transaction
tools.description: Attach an invoice/receipt to the matching bank transaction in NivaDesk. The document can come from the chat (`receipt`), from a link you found for the user — including an attachment in their email or a hosted invoice page (`receiptUrl`) — or, when the invoice is only in an email body, from the message itself (`emailReceipt`). When the user asks to file the invoices sitting in their mail, read each one, then call this tool per invoice; NivaDesk matches it to the bank transaction by amount and date. NivaDesk OCRs images itself; for PDFs (or to help matching) also pass the total amount, the document date (YYYY-MM-DD) and the merchant name you read from the document. If NivaDesk finds one confident match it attaches the file immediately; if several transactions could match it returns candidates with an inboxPath — show them to the user, then call again with the chosen transactionId and the same inboxPath (no need to resend the file). Workspace owner only. Do not ask for companyId. If nothing matches yet, NivaDesk keeps the receipt waiting and attaches it automatically when the payment reaches the bank feed.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

receipt.description: The invoice/receipt file the user attached (image or PDF).

receiptUrl.description: https link to the invoice PDF/image when the user did not attach a file — e.g. an attachment link from their email, or a hosted invoice page (Stripe, Adobe, Shopify). NivaDesk downloads it and stores it as the receipt.

emailReceipt.description: Use when the invoice only exists as an email (no attachment): NivaDesk saves the message itself as the receipt document. Also pass amount/date/merchant when you can read them.

fileName.description: Optional file name for a receiptUrl download.

inboxPath.description: Returned by a previous call when several candidates matched; pass it back together with transactionId instead of resending the file.

transactionId.description: Bank transaction to attach to, when the user has chosen one of the candidates (or named the transaction).

amount.description: Total amount printed on the document, if you can read it.

date.description: Document/payment date YYYY-MM-DD, if you can read it.

merchant.description: Merchant/supplier name on the document, if you can read it.

tools.name: attach_bank_receipt
tools.title: Attach receipt to a bank transaction
tools.description: Attach an invoice/receipt the user shared in the chat to the matching bank transaction in NivaDesk. Pass the user's file as `receipt`. If the photo shows a physical item rather than a document, use create_inventory_item instead. NivaDesk OCRs images itself; for PDFs (or to help matching) also pass the total amount, the document date (YYYY-MM-DD) and the merchant name you read from the document. tools.name: create_inventory_item

Look at the photo, say what you think it is (name, category, brand/model, condition) and ask the user to confirm or correct it, along with anything the photo cannot tell you: how many, and the purchase price. Only after they agree, call this with confirmed:true; pass the same photo as `photo` so it is stored on the item. IMPORTANT: this is for physical stock only. quantity.description: How many, for quantity items. Ask the user; do not guess from the photo.

unit.description: Unit for quantity items, e.g. pcs, m, g.

tools.name: create_order
tools.title: Create order
tools.description: Create a new NivaDesk order in the currently connected workspace. Use the connected workspace automatically. Do not ask for companyId. If the user provides a delivery due date, always pass it as deliveryDueDate in YYYY-MM-DD format. For an already overdue active order, also collect and pass its original created date as paymentDate so Timeline & Delivery and overdue calculations remain accurate. Use this only after the user provides enough order details or confirms creating a draft order. The workspace's own notification rules run on this change: it can send the customer an e-mail or SMS. Say so before you do it.

companyId.description: Workspace/company ID where the order should be created.

watchModel.description: Watch model or reference, for example Rolex Datejust 41.

designBrief.description: Short design brief or customer request.

paidAmount.description: Already paid amount, for example deposit amount.

paymentDate.description: Order created/intake date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Required when creating an already overdue active order.

deliveryDueDate.description: Preferred delivery due date field in YYYY-MM-DD format. Always pass this field when the user provides a delivery date.

dueDate.description: Legacy alias for deliveryDueDate in YYYY-MM-DD format. Prefer deliveryDueDate.

deliveryDays.description: Alternative only when no calendar due date was provided: number of days from created date until due.

tools.name: search_orders
tools.title: Search orders
tools.description: Search orders in the currently connected workspace by customer name, email, watch model, status, order ID, or keyword. Use the connected workspace automatically. Do not ask for companyId.

companyId.description: Workspace/company ID to search.

query.description: Search keyword, customer name, email, watch model, or order ID.

limit.description: Maximum number of orders to return. Default is 10.

tools.name: get_order_detail
tools.title: Get order detail
tools.description: Get full safe order details for one order in the currently connected workspace. Use the connected workspace automatically. Do not ask for companyId.

companyId.description: Workspace/company ID.

tools.name: add_order_note
tools.title: Add order note
tools.description: Append an internal note to an existing order in the currently connected workspace. This is an order note, not a personal Notes item. Do not ask for companyId.

companyId.description: Workspace/company ID.

tools.name: update_order_status
tools.title: Update order status
tools.description: Update an order status or design status in the currently connected workspace. Do not ask for companyId. Use only when the user clearly asks to update the order. The workspace's own notification rules run on this change: it can send the customer an e-mail or SMS. Say so before you do it.

companyId.description: Workspace/company ID.

tools.name: create_note
tools.title: Create personal note
tools.description: Create a new personal Notes item for the connected user in the currently connected workspace. Do not ask for companyId. This is not an order note. Collaboration is not changed automatically.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

tools.name: search_notes
tools.title: Search personal notes
tools.description: Search the connected user's personal Notes in the currently connected workspace. Do not ask for companyId.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

query.description: Keyword to search in title, text, labels or note ID.

limit.description: Maximum number of notes to return. Default is 20.

tools.name: get_note_detail
tools.title: Get personal note detail
tools.description: Get one personal note by note ID from the currently connected workspace. Do not ask for companyId.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

tools.name: append_note
tools.title: Append to personal note
tools.description: Append text to an existing personal note for the connected user in the currently connected workspace. Do not ask for companyId. This is not an order note.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

text.description: Text to append to the note.

tools.name: update_note
tools.title: Update personal note
tools.description: Update the title, text, labels, links or color of a personal note in the currently connected workspace. Do not ask for companyId.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

tools.name: pin_note
tools.title: Pin or unpin personal note
tools.description: Pin or unpin a personal note in the currently connected workspace. Do not ask for companyId.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

isPinned.description: True to pin, false to unpin.

tools.name: archive_note
tools.title: Archive or unarchive personal note
tools.description: Archive or unarchive a personal note in the currently connected workspace. Do not ask for companyId.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

isArchived.description: True to archive, false to unarchive.

tools.name: get_order_financials
tools.title: Get order financials
tools.description: Read the Financial Info card values for one order. You may provide the orderId, or provide query/orderName/customerName so NivaDesk finds the order in the connected workspace. Do not ask the user for companyId. Requires financial access.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

orderId.description: Optional order document ID when already known.

query.description: Order name, customer name or identifying keyword when orderId is not known, for example Ocean Scene Dial.

orderName.description: Optional order/project name alias when orderId is not known.

customerName.description: Optional customer name when orderId is not known.

tools.name: get_dashboard_summary
tools.title: Get dashboard summary
tools.description: Read the connected workspace dashboard summary. ChatGPT App is available on every plan. Free Demo and Starter return permitted basic finance totals (Received, Base Cost and Basic Balance); Pro and Team can return advanced finance when the user role allows it.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

limit.description: Maximum number of orders to scan. Default is 500.

tools.name: get_extra_spending_overview
tools.title: Get extra spending overview
tools.description: Read permitted spending summary data for the connected workspace. Free Demo and Starter return Base Cost only. Pro and Team may include Shipping, Platform Fee, VAT / Tax and custom expenses when the user role allows financial access. Supports thisMonth, thisYear, allTime and customRange.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

scope.description: Optional period: thisMonth, thisYear, allTime, or customRange. Default is thisMonth.

fromDate.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Required only when scope is customRange.

toDate.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Required only when scope is customRange.

includeBaseCost.description: Include Base Cost / watch purchase price. Default true.

includeTax.description: Include VAT / tax amount. Default false.

page.description: Page number for entry results. Default 1.

tools.name: get_financial_overview
tools.title: Get financial overview
tools.description: Read workspace-level financial totals, remaining payments, costs and estimated profit. Requires financial access in the connected workspace.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

limit.description: Maximum number of orders to scan. Default is 1000.

tools.name: get_bank_spending_summary
tools.title: Bank spending summary
tools.description: Summarise the connected workspace's business bank feed (Open Banking) for a month or a year: total spent, incoming, change vs the previous period, spending by category, top merchants and recurring subscriptions. Use for questions like 'how much did I spend in July', 'what are my biggest costs this year', 'which subscriptions do I pay monthly'. Requires the Bank Spending permission (workspace owner or a member the owner granted). Do not ask for companyId.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

year.description: Four-digit year. Defaults to the current year.

month.description: 1-12. Defaults to the current month when period is month.

tools.name: search_bank_transactions
tools.title: Search bank transactions
tools.description: List individual bank transactions from the connected workspace's bank feed, filtered by keyword (merchant/description), date range, category, amount range, or missing receipt. Returns the newest first. Requires the Bank Spending permission. Do not ask for companyId.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

query.description: Keyword matched against merchant and description, e.g. amazon, openai.

category.description: Category name as shown in NivaDesk, e.g. Materials, Software, Shipping; use Uncategorised for transactions without a category.

direction.description: out = spending (default), in = incoming, all = both.

withoutReceipt.description: true = only spending that has no receipt/invoice attached yet.

limit.description: Max rows to return (default 20).

tools.name: attach_bank_receipt
tools.title: Attach receipt to a bank transaction
tools.description: Attach an invoice/receipt the user shared in the chat to the matching bank transaction in NivaDesk. Pass the user's file as `receipt`. If the photo shows a physical item rather than a document, use create_inventory_item instead. NivaDesk OCRs images itself; for PDFs (or to help matching) also pass the total amount, the document date (YYYY-MM-DD) and the merchant name you read from the document. If NivaDesk finds one confident match it attaches the file immediately; if several transactions could match it returns candidates with an inboxPath — show them to the user, then call again with the chosen transactionId and the same inboxPath (no need to resend the file). Workspace owner only. Do not ask for companyId. Image receipts are read with Google Vision OCR. Attaching to a transaction that already has a receipt replaces it, and the previous file is deleted.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

receipt.description: The invoice/receipt file the user attached (image or PDF).

inboxPath.description: Returned by a previous call when several candidates matched; pass it back together with transactionId instead of resending the file.

transactionId.description: Bank transaction to attach to, when the user has chosen one of the candidates (or named the transaction).

amount.description: Total amount printed on the document, if you can read it.

date.description: Document/payment date YYYY-MM-DD, if you can read it.

merchant.description: Merchant/supplier name on the document, if you can read it.

tools.name: search_inventory
tools.title: Search inventory
tools.description: Search stock by name, SKU, serial number, brand, model, category or location, and filter by status, low stock, reserved, location or category. Use it before adding something, so an item the workshop already has gets topped up instead of duplicated. A SKU is a search key, not an identity: two different items may share one, and both are returned. Do not ask for companyId.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

query.description: Part of a name, SKU, serial number, brand, model, category or location.

lowStock.description: Only items at or below their low-stock level.

reserved.description: Only items being held for an order.

limit.description: Maximum items to return (default 20).

tools.name: create_inventory_item
tools.title: Add an inventory item
tools.description: Add a physical item to NivaDesk inventory — typically from a photo the user just took. Look at the photo, say what you think it is (name, category, brand/model, condition) and ask the user to confirm or correct it, along with anything the photo cannot tell you: how many, and the purchase price. Only after they agree, call this with confirmed:true; pass the same photo as `photo` so it is stored on the item. IMPORTANT: this is for physical stock only. If the picture is an invoice, receipt or bill, do NOT use this tool — use attach_bank_receipt, which files it against a bank transaction. Workspace roles that can edit orders may use this. Do not ask for companyId.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

confirmed.description: Must be true, and only after the user has seen your reading of the photo and agreed to it.

name.description: What the item is, as the workshop would call it — e.g. "Rolex Oyster bracelet 20mm".

category.description: Category, e.g. Watch, Part, Material, Tool, Packaging.

trackingType.description: unique = one identifiable object (has a serial); quantity = countable stock. Default unique.

quantity.description: How many, for quantity items. Ask the user; do not guess from the photo.

unit.description: Unit for quantity items, e.g. pcs, m, g.

purchasePrice.description: What the workshop paid, per unit. Ask the user; inventory value is based on this.

currentValueEst.description: Optional estimate of today's value (insurance/resale). It does not change inventory value.

serialNumber.description: Serial/reference if it is visible in the photo or the user gives it.

location.description: Where it is kept, e.g. Drawer 3, Safe.

customerOwned.description: true when the item belongs to a customer (held, not owned). It is then valued at zero.

photo.description: The photo of the item the user shared in the chat.

tools.name: search_commerce_orders
tools.title: Search orders across channels
tools.description: Find orders from any channel and see the provider's own status separately from NivaDesk's workflow status: platform status, payment status, fulfilment status, external order id, connection and last sync all stay distinct fields. It reports no amounts at all: no order total, nothing paid or outstanding, no refund, no tax and no currency. Use it when the user names a shop, an external order number or a payment state. Buyer details are withheld for channels whose data policy restricts them. Do not ask for companyId.

companyId.description: Optional. Usually omit this; the connected workspace is used automatically.

query.description: Order number, project number, external order id, customer name or email.

manualSource.description: With source "manual", narrow to where it came from.

workflowStatus.description: NivaDesk's own status word for the order.

platformStatus.description: The shop's own status word, matched as the provider spells it.

fromDate.description: First day of the range, YYYY-MM-DD.

toDate.description: Last day of the range, YYYY-MM-DD.

needsAttention.description: Only orders held for review or already overdue.

limit.description: Maximum orders to return (default 20).
